1-7.ask: Find a missing angle in a right-angled triangle using a value kept at full accuracy.

1-7.when: Multi-step triangle questions, where an early rounded value would spoil the final answer.
1-7.in: The known sides and angles, and the trig ratio you have chosen.
1-7.read: The angle is about 34.9°, found from a stored full-accuracy value.
trap: The angle is about 34.9 radians.
Rounding the side first gives an equally accurate angle.
1-7.check: Degree mode. Reuse the stored answer instead of retyping a rounded one.

1-9.ask: Find an angle in a non-right-angled triangle, knowing two sides and an angle opposite one of them.
1-9.what: Evaluates the sine rule rearranged for an angle.
1-9.when: You know a side and its opposite angle, plus one more side.
1-9.in: The two sides and the known angle, placed as in your rearranged sine rule.
1-9.read: The angle is about 37° to the nearest degree; check whether its obtuse partner is possible too.
trap: The value on screen is the sine of the angle, so inverse sine is still needed.
The only possible angle is always the acute one.
1-9.check: Degree mode. Use inverse sine. Consider the ambiguous case.

1-13.ask: Find a distance across a lake, knowing two sides and the angle between them, and then find another angle.
1-13.what: Evaluates the cosine rule for a side and for an angle.
1-13.when: You know two sides and the included angle, or all three sides.
1-13.in: The side lengths and the included angle.
1-13.read: The calculation on the screen gives about 63.9°, which is the angle at B. The sheet labels it C; the angle at C is about 44.1°.
trap: 63.9 is a length in metres.
The result is the cosine of the angle.
1-13.check: Degree mode. Brackets around the whole numerator and denominator. Check which angle your cosine rule finds: it is the one between the two sides that are added.

2-2.ask: Find the mode, median and mean from a frequency table.
2-2.what: Calculates summary statistics from values and frequencies.
